text:
gpu-monitor-bot: ALERT: node=gpu-node-42 repeated Xid errors (Xid 13) + ECC correctable spikes over 7m. count=18 in 7m. policy_candidate: auto-eject? :warning:

maria: seeing the same in DCGM dashboard. This node has been flapping since the 03:10 maintenance window.

alex: +1 to take it OOS if repeated Xid + ECC within short window. We keep getting subtle model corruptions when those error patterns happen.

jonathan: want to avoid noise. Can we require both: (1) >10 Xid errors in 10m AND (2) ECC correctable > 100 in same window? Also add a refractory period so we don't auto-eject then undo repeatedly.

maria: agree on hysteresis. Proposed rule: if condition met, cordon node immediately, attempt graceful kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data with 5m timeout, then mark node as unschedulable and put a tag for repro/replacement. If drain fails (pods stuck >5m), fall back to force-evict.

kevin: need to handle Slurm nodes too. Our Slurm adapter should set node state=DRRAIN+set GRES unavailable, and trigger a k8s cordon for hybrid clusters. We have runbook for manual replacement but want automation for scale.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident created: #INC-2123 assigned to infra-oncall.

alex: Pasting draft automation snippet for the rule (canary):

```
automation:
  name: flaky-gpu-eject-v1
  trigger:
    metric_checks:
      - name: xid_errors
        window: 600s
        threshold: 10
      - name: ecc_correctable
        window: 600s
        threshold: 100
  actions:
    - type: cordon
    - type: drain
      grace_period: 300s
    - type: mark_for_replacement
    - type: slack_notify
      channel: #eng-infra
  cooldown: 1800s
  max_daily_ejects_per_zone: 2
```

jonathan: +1 but add an allowlist for nodes with recent maintenance (tag: skip-auto-eject) and a rate limit per-az to avoid capacity storms. Also ensure fallback routing: if node is cordoned, route realtime low-latency jobs to dedicated pool.

maria: test plan: 1) simulate Xid bursts with synthetic DCGM emitter on staging, 2) validate drain behavior with GPU-bound jobs in k8s + Slurm, 3) check alert noise on existing dashboards.

kevin: question about telemetry: are we confident our aggregator dedupes infra-level notifications vs driver logs? We should filter transient Xid spikes (<3 errors in 60s) and only surface aggregated counts.

alex: yes aggregator will roll-up per-instance over sliding window and ignore bursts shorter than 90s unless paired with ECC spikes. Implementation detail in PR #278.

maria: can we also add a quick status annotation on the node: annotation/redwood/gpu-eject-reason = "xid+ecc-agg" and include the last sample blob for debugging.

oncall-bot: infra-oncall acknowledged. Suggested action: run the canary rule in "monitor-only" mode for 48h before enabling active drain.

kevin: sounds good. I'll open a PR with the rule + test harness and schedule a rollout to staging tomorrow.

alex: thanks — will add the Slurm integration patch and tests. When we flip to active mode, notify product owners and ops. :thumbsup:
